challenged_assumptions.assumption: ADR-0116 makes M01-P18 the canonical VCS substrate, justifying retirement now.
challenged_assumptions.challenge: ADR-0116 does not exist in Oyatie's docs/decisions/. The local sequence stops at ADR-0114; the only ADR-0116 hits are Bominal inheritance references to a Kafka/outbox decision, not a VCS-substrate decision. PR 13 cites ADR-0116 nine times as the justification for deletion, but the citation is fabricated or premature.
challenged_assumptions.evidence: ls docs/decisions/ADR-011*.md → only 0110..0114 present; grep ADR-0116 → only ADR-0059/0060/0062 (Bominal Kafka inheritance).

challenged_assumptions.assumption: M01-P18 will own the archive-orphan invariant once deployed.
challenged_assumptions.challenge: M01-P18 (admission gate, projected merge state, conflict kernel) is not yet operational and does not even claim to enforce 'no live ref to archived runtime-glue paths'. Projected-merge-state checks future merges; it does not scan living files for inbound refs to retired archive paths. The replacement invariant is asserted but not demonstrated. Retirement is premature: delete the gate AFTER the replacement enforces the same invariant in CI, not before.
challenged_assumptions.evidence: ADR-0118 'Rejected alternatives' claims 'projected-merge-state and conflict-kernel already own the replacement invariant' with zero pointer to where that enforcement lives.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: This is a 'one-time' lane, not a steady-state invariant.
challenged_assumptions.challenge: Four of the five failure modes are steady-state, not one-time: (a) archive copy lands outside expected root, (b) living code references archived path, (c) original re-appears at active path, (d) inbound ref drift. Any future archive cutover (and there will be more — the masterplan has multiple cutovers) re-activates the same invariant. The 'one-time' label is a convenient narrative, not a structural property. Who certifies one-time vs steady-state? The PR doesn't say.
challenged_assumptions.evidence: Original lane spec lists 4 failure modes that are scan-based steady-state invariants over living files.

challenged_assumptions.challenge: An empty no-op binary plus a contract-guard test (assert: no live ref to known archive roots) costs ~10 LOC and preserves the mechanical-prevention guarantee. Full deletion removes the executable contract entirely; if a future agent re-introduces a path under bominal/agents/ultragoal/archive/pre-grit-cutover-2026-05-12/ there is now zero CI signal. ADR-0118 even cites this concern ('an always-empty runner would be false mechanical confidence') but provides no evidence that always-empty is the realistic state vs. always-zero-violations being a load-bearing guarantee.
challenged_assumptions.evidence: ADR-0118 'Rejected alternatives' bullet #1 hand-waves the tombstone option.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: ADR-0108 sunset → deprecation → removal doctrine does not apply because this is a 'one-time' lane.
challenged_assumptions.challenge: ADR-0108 carries no one-time-lane carve-out. The user directive 'sunset > deprecation > removal. dispatch.' is doctrine — applied flat. PR 13 jumps straight to removal with no sunset window, no deprecation period, and no _sunset metadata. The 'no_exceptions_canonical' feedback explicitly forbids exemptions. This violates the canonical lifecycle the repo just scaffolded in oya-governance-sunset-lifecycle-kernel one day prior (2026-05-15 CHANGELOG entry directly above the retirement entry).
challenged_assumptions.evidence: docs/CHANGELOG.md 2026-05-15 entry establishes sunset-lifecycle kernel; 2026-05-16 entry skips it for archive-orphan.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: Removing the workspace member and Cargo.lock entries is the right scope for 'retirement'.
challenged_assumptions.challenge: If the lane is genuinely retired but the historical lane doc and ADR-0118 keep the symbol names (RetiredArchiveDir, RetiredKernel, RetiredApp) as 'ledger-only names', that creates two name-spaces: retired-symbol-as-string vs. removed-crate. Future agents grepping for RetiredKernel will hit a doc with no code. This is a tombstone-without-the-tombstone-file pattern.
challenged_assumptions.evidence: IP-008 diff: 'Retired-symbols' block names symbols that exist only as strings.

missing_considerations: No verification that any other fitness lane (e.g., adapter-with-no-importer, banned-primitives) actually scans for refs to bominal/agents/ultragoal/archive/pre-grit-cutover-2026-05-12 — the replacement invariant is asserted but not located.
No grep across the repo proving zero remaining live refs to the archive path before deletion; the lane itself was the proof, and it is removed in the same PR.
ADR-0118 'supersedes: [ADR-0052]' but ADR-0052 was the inventory ledger driving the cutover — superseding it without replacement of the inventory contract leaves the cutover ledger orphaned.
No sunset_date / removal_date pair as the new oya-governance-sunset-lifecycle-kernel would require.
verdict_justification: Load-bearing citation ADR-0116 does not exist locally in Oyatie. The retirement is justified by a phantom ADR. Combined with skipping the just-scaffolded sunset-lifecycle doctrine and asserting replacement invariants without locating them, this PR is built on three unverified loads. REJECT until: (1) the actual local ADR establishing M01-P18 as canonical VCS substrate is cited (or created), (2) the replacement-invariant location is named with file:line, (3) the sunset-lifecycle workflow is honored or an explicit ADR-0108 carve-out is written.
escalation_reason: Phantom ADR citation + doctrine bypass triggers systemic-issue threshold.
